checks.check: Migration installs on the production employee storage format
Only an approved account with a unique verified-email match is auto-linked
Public verification preserves leading zeroes and returns no personnel data
Anonymous callers cannot enumerate employee rows or call the private resolver
Direct signup without an encoded employee ID is rejected, including a forged admin flag
The database derives identity from the employee row, links the account and keeps approval pending
A pending request reserves the employee ID against duplicate signup
Pending accounts cannot read attendance
An approved User receives only their linked ceremony/uniform records and allowed record fields
Legacy permissive table policies cannot expose other employees attendance
The existing user directory retains personnel rows without monitoring arrays
A User cannot request a different employee ID or change the authoritative link
Editing Auth user metadata cannot redirect attendance
Unlinked existing accounts receive an empty link state with no fallback to another employee
Administrator employee encoding access remains available, with no personal attendance endpoint
Trusted existing Admin account creation works without public-registration employee fields
An employee without a recorded email can submit a pending request for administrator review
Deleting a linked employee cannot silently orphan or redirect the account
Employee-number corrections preserve the stable account/attendance link
An active Admin can explicitly link a verified existing User to the encoded employee
Anonymous row access remains blocked even with a legacy PUBLIC grant and read policy
Ambiguous employee numbers are rejected instead of selecting a different person
The migration is repeatable without deleting or relinking records
